events.title: Bennington Vets Town Hall (2026)
events.description:
at

Free and open to all.

Presented by the Vermont Veterans Home. Emceed by ISG (Retired) Frank Wetherby.

All are invited to a Vets Town Hall in the A. Luke Crisp Room at the Vermont Veterans Home on Friday, November 6th, at 6pm in Bennington, Vermont. Veterans are invited to speak about what their service means to them. Non-veterans are encouraged to attend and listen. This event is free, non-political, and all perspectives are valued. There will be no debate on American foreign policy.

RSVPs are optional, but encouraged. Light refreshments will be available.

Register as a speaker or attendee

What to Expect

For all attendees: All community members are invited to this event. Only veterans will speak, but non-veterans are encouraged to attend and listen. Throughout the event, you may hear something you agree or disagree with. You may have a question. Or you may want to say encouraging words with the intention to help. However, we ask that you please refrain from responding. We are simply here to listen and learn about what it was like to serve in the wars that this nation has chosen to fight.

For speakers: Tell us what your service means to you. Please tell us about your own experiences, whatever they may be, rather than speaking broadly about an issue or organization. You’re a member of our community, and it’s your stories, reflections, and insights that we’re anxious to hear. If you’re interested in speaking but aren’t sure what to speak about, click here for some questions that can serve as starting points. Each veteran will be given up to 10 minutes to speak. Veterans who would like to speak can mark that preference when registering. If you’re considering speaking but prefer not to register, we encourage you to attend. After pre-registered speakers go, the host will take speakers from the floor, time permitting. The goal is for every veteran who would like to speak to have a chance to do so. Of course, veterans (and all community members) are also welcome to simply attend and listen.

Getting There

The event will take place in the A. Luke Crisp Room.

The best parking for this event is in the rear of the building, using the Park Street entrance. Please use the entrance at the Chapel of the Four Chaplains.

The building is accessible.

events.title: Hanover, NH Vets Town Hall (2026)
events.description:
at

Free and open to all

Presented by VERN at Dartmouth College

All are invited to a Vets Town Hall in the Georgiopoulos classroom at Tuck LLC – Raether at Dartmouth College on Tuesday, November 10th, at 6pm in Hanover, New Hampshire. Veterans are invited to speak about what their service means to them. Non-veterans are encouraged to attend and listen. This event is free, non-political, and all perspectives are valued. There will be no debate on American foreign policy.

Register as a speaker or attendee

What to Expect

For all attendees: All community members are invited to this event. Only veterans will speak, but non-veterans are encouraged to attend and listen. Throughout the event, you may hear something you agree or disagree with. You may have a question. Or you may want to say encouraging words with the intention to help. However, we ask that you please refrain from responding. We are simply here to listen and learn about what it was like to serve in the wars that this nation has chosen to fight.

For speakers: Tell us what your service means to you. Please tell us about your own experiences, whatever they may be, rather than speaking broadly about an issue or organization. You’re a member of our community, and it’s your stories, reflections, and insights that we’re anxious to hear. If you’re interested in speaking but aren’t sure what to speak about, click here for some questions that can serve as starting points. Each veteran will be given up to 10 minutes to speak. Veterans who would like to speak can mark that preference when registering. If you’re considering speaking but prefer not to register, we encourage you to attend. After pre-registered speakers go, the host will take speakers from the floor, time permitting. The goal is for every veteran who would like to speak to have a chance to do so. Of course, veterans (and all community members) are also welcome to simply attend and listen.

Getting There

Directions:
If coming from I-91, you will take Exit 13 towards Hanover. After you cross Ledyard Bridge into Hanover, you will come to a stop light where you will turn left. When you drive up the hill, Channing Cox Parking lot will be on your left. 

If coming from I-89, you will take Exit 18 for Route 120. Take Route 120 into Hanover where you will go through town and leave town towards Vermont down W Wheelock St. At the bottom of W Wheelock, you will come to a stop light where you will take a right up the hill and at the top, Channing Cox parking lot will be on your left.

From the parking lot, follow signs made directing attendees to the Vets Town Hall. It is a short walk from the parking lot to the building. Once inside the building, make your way downstairs to the room. There are both stairs and elevator to get downstairs.

Parking: Parking for the event will be located at the Channing Cox parking lot. Overflow parking will be in the ECSC parking garage (a pin will be provided to gain access) and accessible parking will be in front of the venue. If you type in “Channing Cox Lot Hanover NH” into your GPS, it should bring you to the parking area. (You will pass the parking garage on your way up to Channing Cox Lot.)

Accessibility: The venue is fully accessible. There is accessible parking in front of the venue. If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to [contact omitted] at least a week ahead of the event.

    Jason Mosel

    Jason Mosel is a Network Engineer at Dartmouth College and a United States Marine Corp Veteran. Jason served as a TOW gunner from 2003-2007 completing three deployments including two to Iraq. Jason is an avid runner, homesteader, and veteran advocate. He started the Veteran Employee Resource Network at Dartmouth College in 2020 and continues to…

    VERN at Dartmouth College

    The Veterans ERN provides a welcoming community for all employees who have served in the Armed Forces, current service members, military spouses or partners, family members of veterans, and all others dedicated to honoring and supporting the military community.

events.description:
at

Free and open to all

Presented by Town Hall Theater. Cathy Turner will emcee.

All are invited to attend a Family Vets Town Hall, on Thursday, November 12th at 5:30pm at Town Hall Theater in Middlebury. Immediate family members of veterans are invited to stand before their community and speak for up to ten minutes about their experiences. Everyone is encouraged to attend and listen. The event is free and non-political, and all perspectives are valued. RSVPs are optional but encouraged.

Register as a speaker or attendee

What to Expect

For all attendees: All community members are invited to this event. Only immediate family members of veterans will speak, but all are encouraged to attend and listen. Throughout the event, you may hear something you agree or disagree with. You may have a question. Or you may want to say encouraging words with the intention to help. However, we ask that you please refrain from responding. We are simply here to listen and learn.

For speakers: Please tell us about your own experiences, whatever they may be, rather than speaking broadly about an issue or organization. You’re a member of our community, and it’s your stories, reflections, and insights that we’re anxious to hear. Each speaker will be given up to 10 minutes. Family members of veterans who would like to speak can mark that preference when registering. If you’re considering speaking but prefer not to register, we encourage you to attend. After pre-registered speakers go, the emcee will take speakers from the floor, time permitting. Of course, family members of veterans (and all community members) are also welcome to simply attend and listen.

Getting There

Directions & Parking
Find directions and parking info here.

Accessibility
The venue is accessible. You can find additional information here.
